title: Canonical derived ringed-topos adjunction is shift-compatible
statement: Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small ringed sites with sheaves of commutative rings $R_X,R_Y$ and structure map $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$, and let $L=Lf^*$ and $R=Rf_*$ be the canonical derived functors [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] constructed from K-flat [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and K-injective resolutions [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] with the derived adjunction [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] $L\dashv R$, unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$. Equip $L$ and $R$ with the canonical integer-shift comparisons in the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] obtained by shifting the chosen K-flat and K-injective resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift]. Then the derived adjunction is compatible with these comparisons in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique]: for every integer $n$, the unit and counit commute with shift, and the shift comparison on $R$ is the unique one compatible with the unit and the fixed shift comparison on $L$.

proof.text: Use the right Kan extension universal property in hL. For arbitrary Q, F, LF and comparison alpha, postcomposing LF with a right adjoint S preserves the equality test for transformations into LF: transpose each transformation through T adjoint S, use the right Kan extension equality test, and transpose back. Naturality of the counit identifies the tested composites with gamma followed by S(alpha). This is the proved private helper rightKan_postadjoint_ext; no resolution choices are required.

Apply that equality test also after postcomposition by each shift equivalence. If alpha and the image (Q tau) followed by S(alpha) commute with shifts, compare the two sides of the shift square of tau after the test. Precompose with H of the invertible shift comparison of Q. Naturality of tau moves that comparison to the target; the shift squares of the image and of S(alpha) identify the composites. Cancel the comparison. The private helper rightKan_postadjoint_commShift formalizes this argument for every integer.

Let ah be the termwise homotopy adjunction induced by adj0. Its unit commutes with shifts: on complexes this is the degreewise underived unit, and the identity descends through the homotopy quotient. The existing source-library instance commShift_mapHomotopyCategory_unit supplies this fact. Specialize the given normalization to M, Fh(M), and the identity map. The homEquiv unit formula yields eta(Q M) followed by R(alpha_M) equal to Q(eta0_M) followed by beta_(Fh M).

Express that equality as equality of natural transformations. Its right side is a composite of the localized termwise unit, beta whiskered by Fh, and canonical associators and unitors; each commutes with shifts. Apply the preceding universal-property helper with Q=Qh, LF=L, S=R, T=L, tau=eta, using hL, to prove that the derived unit commutes with all integer shifts. This proves CompatibilityUnit for the fixed comparisons. The right-derived universal property and resolution invertibility are unnecessary because the normalized beta is already an input. The proved private helper normalized_unit_commShift carries out this composition argument before specialization to sheaf-module categories, avoiding expansion of their large types during elaboration.

Apply compatibilityCounit_of_compatibilityUnit to obtain counit compatibility for every integer. Apply compatibilityUnit_unique_right to any other right comparison satisfying the unit equation to obtain equality with the fixed comparison, without any extra coherence hypothesis.
